messages:
alex: heads-up — I'm sketching a small change to the cost dashboard sampling that might affect per-SKU latency/cost curves. thinking out loud: we currently sample 1/100 invocations for token-cost attribution which loses signal for low-volume but high-latency SKUs. :thinking:
jess: yes i've seen that — small tenants with chat chains spike apparent cost variance because sampling misses heavy-tail long-context calls. what's your proposal?
alex: idea: make sampling stratified by (sku, latency_bucket). basically keep baseline 1/100, but upsample invocations where p50>200ms or token_count>1024. would preserve overall rate but increase representation for expensive tails.
matt: curious how we'd implement without blowing ingestion. can we do it in the router where we already tag latency? or do we need a second sampler in the collector?
daria: router has a tiny sampling hook but it runs pre-response so no token_count yet. collector has full record but is post-hoc and harder to control per-sku budgets. maybe do a hybrid: router marks candidate for upsample if request hint (like client-provided expected_tokens) present, otherwise collector backfills using slow-latency predicate.
zoe: how do we avoid biasing rollouts? if we upsample high-latency, dashboards may look worse after we change sampling and product teams will freak. need a clear migration note and toggle.
alex: agreed. plan: 1) implement stratified sampler behind a feature flag 2) produce a pair of views for a few days: raw sampled view vs. reweighted estimate that preserves old weighting (so teams can see delta caused by sampling change) 3) add an explainability banner: "sampling policy changed on X — see migration comparison"
jess: also need to credit cache savings correctly — currently prefetch/cache-hit tokens are often attributed to caller sku but are shared across routes. Does the upsampling affect cache-savings apportionment?
matt: yes it could. If we over-index on high-latency invocations that tend to be cold (no cache), we'll underreport amortized cache savings. We should compute cache-savings at the session level and then attach to invocations with proportional weights.
daria: quick pseudo: 
```
# sampling decision (router)
if hint.expected_tokens > 1024: sample_weight *= 10
if last_call_latency > 200: sample_weight *= 5
```
then collector emits record with sample_weight and cache_hits, model_sku, route_id. aggregation engine uses sum(sample_weight*cost) / sum(sample_weight)
zoe: and quotas? sampling tweaks shouldn't change quota enforcement. but reported per-route cost numbers will change and could trigger alerts. we should route historical alerts through a diff check.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/stratified-sampler -> canary group eng-platform at 2024-11-08T09:00:00Z. :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks ops-bot. next steps: I'll open a PR for the router flag + collector field; matt can you prototype the reweighting UI with a compare toggle? jess/daria can you review attribution logic? i'll draft migration note for console.
matt: yeah i'll mock the UI. suggestion: show both series (old-estimate, stratified-estimate) and a "sampling-impact" sparkline. keep default to old-estimate for 48h then flip.
jess: adding one ask — make the sampling config queryable via internal API so SRE can reproduce sampling decisions for specific invocations (debugging).
daria: ack, we can expose /internal/sampling/debug?ts=... returning sample_weight components. small perf hit but only on debug calls.
zoe: timeline? if canary goes well, roll to 50% in 24h and full after 72h. communicate to product and CS before flip.
alex: perfect. i'll create the RFC and PR today. tagging @matt @jess @daria for followups. :rocket:
